children: and its partners in the LNG Canada export project could reach a final investment ‌decision on its Phase 2 expansion as early as next month, Reuters reported Thursday.
The expansion would add 14M ​metric tons/year of liquefied natural gas export capacity ​to the facility in British Columbia, effectively doubling the ⁠project's total capacity to 28M tons/year.
LNG Canada, a joint venture led by Shell
and ​backed by Malaysia's Petronas, PetroChina, Mitsubishi, and Korea Gas, ​is Canada's first large-scale LNG export terminal.
The ⁠project's C$40B Phase 1 facility shipped its first ⁠cargo ​earlier this year and is considered a cornerstone of Canada's effort to become a major global LNG exporter.
